definitions.explanation: A man married to one's mother who is not one's biological father.

examples.japanese: {義父|ぎふ}は{会社|かいしゃ}を{経営|けいえい}している。
{義父|ぎふ}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{釣|つ}りに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went fishing together with my father-in-law.

examples.japanese: {結婚|けっこん}して{初|はじ}めて{義父|ぎふ}に{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met my father-in-law for the first time after getting married.

notes:
TERMS OF ADDRESS:
While {義父|ぎふ} is the formal/written term, in conversation people typically address their father-in-law as:
・お{義父|とう}さん - most common
・{義|ぎ}のお{父|とう}さん - explicit "in-law's father"

CONTEXT:
{義父|ぎふ} is more commonly used in:
・Written documents
・Speaking about (not to) one's father-in-law
・Formal contexts

FAMILY TERMS WITH {義|ぎ}:
・{義母|ぎぼ} - mother-in-law
・{義兄|ぎけい} - brother-in-law (older)
・{義弟|ぎてい} - brother-in-law (younger)
・{義姉|ぎし} - sister-in-law (older)
・{義妹|ぎまい} - sister-in-law (younger)

NUANCE:
The {義|ぎ} prefix indicates a family relationship through marriage rather than blood.
